zh.summary: 把同一任務的現況、目標與例外路徑並列，讓缺漏回復、交接條件和系統邊界能被逐步討論。
objectives: 為同一任務寫出有角色、起點與終點的 As-Is 與 To-Be。
用分支表與主流程表示缺漏、修改後重查及取消路徑。
區分使用者操作流程、整體旅程與系統架構。

readingGuide.goal: 為同一任務寫出有角色、起點與終點的 As-Is 與 To-Be。
readingGuide.startingPoint: problem.md、文字編輯器或紙筆，以及四張合成事件卡；不必安裝繪圖軟體。
readingGuide.route: 先看情境與原理，再比較例子，最後擴寫 problem.md 並用檢核題自查。
readingGuide.output: problem.md 具有可比較的兩條流程、主路徑與三個例外分支，以及明確原型邊界。

sections.heading: AASE M03-03｜As-Is、To-Be 與 User Flow：如何把工作流程變成真正好用的軟體？
paragraphs: 開發軟體之前，先弄清楚人們原本怎麼完成工作、希望以後怎麼完成，以及過程中發生問題時該怎麼辦。
無論你想開發的是醫院掛號系統、工廠管理平台、電商網站、銀行內部工具，還是 AI Agent，都應該先理解三個概念：

- As-Is（現況流程）：現在這件事是怎麼做的？
- To-Be（目標流程）：未來希望怎麼做得更好？
- User Flow（使用者操作流程）：使用者在新系統中，要經過哪些操作、判斷和分支，才能完成任務？
三者的關係可以用一句話表示：
As-Is 幫助我們發現問題，To-Be 幫助我們設計改進，User Flow 幫助我們確認新方法真的走得通。
這也是為什麼開發軟體不能一開始就只問：「我們要用 React、Python，還是什麼 AI 模型？」技術只是實現手段，真正要先確定的是工作本身。

sections.heading: 一、先從日常生活理解這三個概念
paragraphs: 假設你經營一家餐廳，每天早上都必須向食材供應商訂貨。
As-Is：目前的工作方式
店長每天查看冰箱，用紙記錄缺少的食材，再打電話給供應商。對方如果沒接電話，就得稍後再打。
問題：耗時、容易漏訂、沒有完整紀錄。
To-Be：希望改進後的方式
店長打開訂貨系統，系統顯示庫存和建議採購量，店長確認數量後送出訂單，供應商收到通知。
目標：減少重複作業、降低漏訂機率、保留紀錄。
User Flow：實際上要怎麼操作？
店長登入 → 檢查庫存 → 調整訂貨量 → 確認 → 送出。
但是如果食材缺貨、價格變動、網路中斷，或店長臨時取消呢？這些都需要明確的操作路徑。
注意：上面的 To-Be 只是設計假設，不是已經證明會改善績效。真正上線前，還需要驗證資料是否正確、店長是否願意採用，以及新的作法有沒有增加額外負擔。

blocks.caption: 圖 1｜餐廳訂貨的三種描述
blocks.description: 箭頭表示分析從現況走向目標與具體操作；改善仍是待驗證假設。

items.title: As-Is
items.body: 查看冰箱 → 紙本記錄缺料 → 打電話；未接通要重撥。問題是耗時、漏訂與紀錄不完整。

items.title: To-Be
items.body: 呈現庫存與建議量 → 店長確認 → 送出 → 通知供應商。目標為減少重工、漏訂並留存紀錄；通知不等於供應商接受。

items.title: User Flow
items.body: 登入 → 檢查庫存 → 調整數量 → 確認 → 送出；缺貨、變價、斷線與取消另有分支。

paragraphs: 這就是需求工程（Requirements Engineering）的精神：不要只想像一個漂亮的系統，要了解它能否改善真實工作。

sections.heading: 二、第一個重要原則：比較之前，先確定起點與終點
paragraphs: 先固定比較範圍，才能判讀流程是否改善。
想像兩個人比較從台北到高雄的交通方式。
甲說：「我開車要四小時。」
乙說：「我搭高鐵只要一個半小時。」
但是甲計算的是從家門口開到目的地，乙只算高鐵列車在軌道上行駛的時間，完全沒算往返車站。
這樣比較公平嗎？當然不公平。
比較工作流程也一樣。
假設醫院要改善病人掛號流程：

blocks.caption: 二、第一個重要原則：比較之前，先確定起點與終點｜比較表
rows: 打電話、查詢時間、確認資訊
線上選科別、時間、確認資訊
取得有效掛號結果或取消
取得有效掛號結果或取消

paragraphs: 兩邊必須處理同一個任務，才能合理比較時間、成本、錯誤率和完成率。
如果 As-Is 包含電話接通、醫院審核、報到及看診，而 To-Be 只包含點擊「預約」按鈕，那就不是公平比較。

blocks.heading: 定義任務的五個要素
paragraphs: 任務定義 = 角色 + 起點 + 終點 + 成功條件 + 範圍
以線上掛號為例
角色（Actor）： 要掛號的病人
起點（Trigger）： 病人想預約某次門診
終點（End State）： 掛號成功取得確認資訊，或取消
成功條件（Success Condition）： 系統確實建立有效預約，病人能確認預約內容
範圍（Scope）： 包含預約操作，不包含後續診斷與治療
這五個要素是實用的任務定義框架，不是某一套強制性的標準。
尤其要注意：使用者看見「成功」訊息，不代表實際業務已成功。 系統還必須有相應證據，例如掛號紀錄確實建立。

sections.heading: 三、As-Is：不只是記錄步驟，而是弄清楚現實中的工作
paragraphs: As-Is 可以理解為「工作現場的紀錄」。
假設工廠每次設備故障，都要由維修人員處理：

1. 現場作業員發現設備異常。
2. 打電話通知主管。
3. 主管聯絡維修部門。
4. 維修人員到現場判斷。
5. 維修完成後填寫紙本紀錄。
6. 主管確認設備可以恢復運轉。
這是一條可能的 As-Is 流程。
但如果只記錄這六個步驟，你仍然不知道很多重要事情。
例如：主管不在怎麼辦？維修人員沒有零件怎麼辦？故障重複發生，誰能查到前次紀錄？設備沒有完成安全確認，是否可能被誤開機？
這些看似枝微末節的情況，其實往往是開發系統的真正理由。

blocks.heading: 怎麼取得可信的 As-Is？
paragraphs: 你可以從三種證據逐步建立：

blocks.caption: 三、As-Is：不只是記錄步驟，而是弄清楚現實中的工作｜比較表
rows: 不代表現場都如此執行
他們認為如何完成工作
實際怎麼做、在哪裡卡住
需要考量觀察範圍與代表性

paragraphs: 因此，要把「已觀察到的現況」與「我們推測的現況」分開。
例如：
「工廠通常需要主管簽核才能報修。」
如果沒有訪談、紀錄或制度支持，應標示為待確認假設，不能直接寫成已經核實的事實。
這與英國 GOV.UK 的服務探索（Discovery）方法一致：在投入建置前，先理解使用者的工作、現有制度、限制，以及服務與其他部門的關係。

sections.heading: 四、To-Be：不是把所有工作自動化，而是重新設計更好的工作方式
paragraphs: 假設剛才工廠的維修系統準備引入 AI。
一個直覺想法可能是：
「讓 AI 自動判斷故障、自動安排維修、自動決定是否恢復生產。」
問題在於，這把許多不同性質的責任全部交給 AI。
更合適的 To-Be 可能是：

blocks.caption: 四、To-Be：不是把所有工作自動化，而是重新設計更好的工作方式｜比較表
headers: 系統或 AI 的責任
rows: AI 提供可能原因與歷史紀錄
系統顯示可用人力與零件
授權人員確認安全條件

paragraphs: 這裡存在三個層次：
第一層：資訊改善。 原本資訊散落在電話、紙本與個人記憶中，現在集中呈現。
第二層：工作改善。 原本需要人工反覆查詢，現在系統能更快提供需要的資料。
第三層：決策改善。 AI 可以協助提出建議，但高風險決策仍由具備權限與責任的人員確認。
因此，設計 To-Be 時可以問：
「哪些工作應該消除？哪些可以簡化？哪些適合自動化？哪些必須保留人工？」
還要問一個問題：原本的步驟是否具有安全、法律或品質上的必要性？
不是每個看似多餘的步驟都應該刪掉。這也是為什麼 To-Be 不能只追求流程最短。

sections.heading: 五、User Flow：真正把系統操作畫清楚
paragraphs: 前面我們談的是工作方式。
現在進一步聚焦到：使用者操作軟體時會遇到什麼？
教材使用的範例是一個「欄位完整性檢查」原型。使用者輸入申請編號、申請人代號及文件類型，系統檢查必要欄位有沒有缺漏，最後產出完整性報告。
這裡特別要區分：

- 完整性（Completeness）：必要欄位是不是都有填？
- 正確性（Correctness）：所填內容是不是正確？
- 真實性（Authenticity）：相關資料是否真實可信？
- 正式受理（Acceptance）：業務是否依規定接受這個案件？
系統檢查「三個欄位都有填寫」，只能證明符合指定的欄位完整性規則，不能直接證明資料正確，也不能代表審核通過。

blocks.heading: 用流程圖理解
paragraphs: To-Be User Flow：完整性檢查原型
以下將教材的成功路徑與例外處理整合為一張示意圖。

blocks.caption: 圖 2｜完整性檢查：判斷與回復
blocks.description: 依每個判斷的明列出口走讀；回填保留資料，修改使舊結果失效。箭頭表示控制流程，不代表經過時間或業務核准。

items.title: 開始
items.body: → 輸入必要欄位。

items.title: 輸入必要欄位
items.body: 申請編號、申請人代號、文件類型 → 是否取消？

items.title: 是否取消？
items.body: 是 → 結束：不產生報告。否 → 檢查目前輸入。

items.title: 檢查目前輸入
items.body: → 欄位完整？

items.title: 欄位完整？
items.body: 否 → 提示缺漏並保留已填資料。是 → 預覽檢查結果。

items.title: 提示缺漏並保留已填資料
items.body: → 輸入必要欄位，補齊後重新檢查。

items.title: 預覽檢查結果
items.body: → 是否修改資料？

items.title: 是否修改資料？
items.body: 是 → 使原檢查結果失效。否 → 是否確認匯出？

items.title: 使原檢查結果失效
items.body: → 輸入必要欄位，必須重新檢查。

items.title: 是否確認匯出？
items.body: 是 → 匯出完整性報告 → 任務完成。否／取消 → 結束：不產生報告。

items.title: 匯出完整性報告 → 任務完成
items.body: 報告對應目前已檢查輸入；不代表正式受理。

items.title: 結束：不產生報告
items.body: 本次不產生新報告；草稿保留規則另行決定。

paragraphs: 閱讀時請先看判斷節點中的條件，以及每種結果要去哪裡。

blocks.caption: User Flow 裡經常出現的專有名詞
rows: 誰正在操作或參與任務
使用者或系統做了什麼
一切符合預期時怎麼完成
發生缺漏或其他異常時怎麼辦
出問題後如何回到可繼續的狀態
成功、取消、失敗或其他明確結果

paragraphs: 其中，Happy Path 只代表正常情況，不代表系統的全部行為。
假設你設計購物網站：
正常情況是「選商品 → 購物車 → 付款 → 下單成功」。
但付款失敗、庫存不足、折價券過期、使用者放棄結帳等情況，通通不能從流程中消失。

sections.heading: 六、最值得深入理解的概念：修改資料後，舊結果為什麼必須失效？
paragraphs: 這是 M03-03 特別重要的一個設計原則，也是 AI 軟體開發中很常見的錯誤來源。
假設保險公司有一套 AI 報價系統。
使用者先輸入：

blocks.caption: 圖 3｜第一次試算的輸入與結果
blocks.description: 合成範例：數字用來辨認結果對應哪次輸入，不是保費公式。

items.title: 試算結果：已產生
items.body: 對應原輸入；改為 300 萬元時，此結果失效。

paragraphs: 接著，使用者把保障額度改成 300 萬元。
如果系統的畫面已經顯示 300 萬，但下載的 PDF 仍然是先前 100 萬元的報價內容，會發生什麼問題？
使用者看到的輸入資料與輸出的文件不一致。
這稱為 Stale Result（過期結果） 問題。
解決方式不是單純更新畫面，而是讓每一份結果與產生它的輸入保持一致。

blocks.heading: 結果失效模擬
paragraphs: 修改 → 失效 → 重新檢查 → 輸出。
你可以將這種設計理解成一條約束：
結果有效 ⇒ 目前輸入與已驗證輸入一致。
實務上不能只依靠一個前端的「已檢查」標記。若資料會在多人或多系統間變更，還需要在後端透過版本號、資料快照或雜湊等方式確認一致性，並且在真正執行操作時再次驗證。
這個原則可以應用到許多產業。

blocks.caption: 六、最值得深入理解的概念：修改資料後，舊結果為什麼必須失效？｜比較表
headers: 資料修改後可能發生的問題
rows: 客戶修改貸款金額，但報告使用舊資料
使舊計算與審核結果失效
病人資料更新後，仍顯示舊風險分析
修改購物車後仍保留舊結帳金額
收件地址改變，但運費是依舊地址計算
使用者修改任務要求，Agent 卻沿用舊計畫執行
重新檢查計畫與執行授權

paragraphs: 這是從流程設計一路延伸到軟體狀態管理、資料一致性與安全治理的重要連結。

sections.heading: 七、User Flow、User Journey、System Architecture 到底有什麼不同？
paragraphs: 這三種圖常被混在一起，但它們回答的是不同問題。
User Flow｜使用者操作流程
關注一個具體任務：使用者點哪裡、做什麼、遇到問題怎麼回復。
例如：病人如何在掛號網站完成一次預約。
User Journey / Experience Map｜使用者旅程／經驗地圖
關注一段較長的經驗，可能跨越不同時間、人物、場所與服務。
例如：病人從發現不舒服、尋找醫院、掛號、就診，到後續追蹤的整體經驗。
System Architecture｜系統架構
關注技術元件如何協作。
例如：掛號網站如何呼叫 API、資料庫如何儲存預約、身分驗證怎麼運作，以及系統如何防止重複預約。

blocks.caption: 圖 5｜不同問題，使用不同觀點
blocks.description: 三種觀點並列比較，不是依序執行的三個步驟。

items.title: User Flow
items.body: 單一任務：病人完成一次掛號的操作、判斷與回復。

items.title: User Journey / Experience Map
items.body: 較長經驗：不舒服 → 找醫院 → 掛號 → 看診 → 追蹤，跨越人物、場所與服務。

items.title: System Architecture
items.body: 技術協作：網站、API、預約資料庫、身分驗證與防重複預約控制。

paragraphs: 這裡還可以補充 Swimlane Diagram（泳道流程圖），它會用不同泳道來區分各角色或部門的責任，例如病人、掛號系統、醫院櫃台。
更正式的跨組織作業流程，也可能使用 BPMN（Business Process Model and Notation，企業流程模型與標記法）。
但不需要一開始就學完所有圖表標準。
本課先把「使用者要完成什麼、如何完成、遇到例外怎麼辦」講清楚就夠了。
GOV.UK 的 Experience Map 指南也指出，旅程地圖可以納入使用者在不同時間點的行為、想法、感受與跨服務接觸，不等同於單一系統的操作圖。

sections.heading: 八、如何將這些觀念真正用在 AI 協作軟體工程？
paragraphs: 最實用的方式，是把分析結果寫成 AI 與人類都能理解的需求文件，例如 `problem.md`。
它不是程式碼，而是未來設計、實作與驗證的依據。
以下回到餐廳訂貨，示範一份簡化版本。

blocks.heading: problem.md
paragraphs: 合成範例；As-Is 待訪談確認，To-Be 待驗證。
blocks.code:
# 任務：建立食材訂貨要求

## 角色
主要使用者：餐廳店長
交接對象：食材供應商

## 任務邊界
起點：店長取得需要訂購的食材清單
終點：訂貨要求已記錄並送出，或取消
不包含：供應商正式接單、送貨與付款

## As-Is（待訪談確認）
1. 店長盤點食材
2. 手寫訂貨清單
3. 打電話提出訂貨要求
4. 記錄已提出的要求

## To-Be（待驗證設計）
1. 選擇食材
2. 輸入訂購數量
3. 系統檢查必填資訊
4. 店長預覽內容
5. 店長確認送出
6. 系統記錄送出結果

## 例外與回復路徑
- 缺漏：提示缺少資訊，保留已填資料
- 修改：使舊預覽失效，重新檢查
- 送出失敗：顯示未確認送出，提供安全重試
- 取消：結束操作，不送出新要求

## 待確認事項
- 供應商能否接收電子訂單？
- 重試是否可能造成重複訂貨？
- 取消後是否保留草稿？
- 供應商接受訂單如何確認？

paragraphs: 這份文件最大的價值，在於你不需要一開始就決定前端框架、資料庫或 AI 模型。
你可以先把它交給 AI Coding Agent，例如 OpenCode，要求它：
「請根據 `problem.md`，整理 User Flow、例外情境與可驗收的需求。不要自行假設供應商已經接單，也不要在未確認需求前擴充正式付款功能。」
這會比單純說「幫我寫一個智慧訂貨網站」更容易控制開發範圍與結果。

blocks.heading: 從流程走向實作的完整關係
paragraphs: 讀圖時請分清楚共同的流程分析，以及介面和規格／測試兩項平行工作。

blocks.caption: 圖 6｜從流程分析走向實作
blocks.description: As-Is → To-Be → User Flow 分向 UI/UX 與需求／測試兩項平行工作，再共同支持實作、驗證與改善；箭頭表示依賴，不強制瀑布式時程。

items.title: As-Is
items.body: 理解目前問題與限制。

items.title: To-Be
items.body: 設計更好的工作方式。

items.title: User Flow
items.body: 定義操作、判斷與例外路徑。

items.title: UI / UX
items.body: M04：設計易用介面。

items.title: 需求規格與測試
items.body: M05 / M08：定義可驗收行為。

items.title: 實作、驗證與改善
items.body: 架構設計、AI Coding、測試與迭代。

paragraphs: 其中，流程設計不會直接決定系統的技術架構，但會提供技術架構必須滿足的行為要求。

sections.heading: 九、學完這一課，如何判斷你真的會用了？
paragraphs: 原始 M03-03 的實作要求，可以整理成一項很實用的驗收方式：拿幾個不同的事件情境，沿著流程走一遍，看看有沒有走不通的地方。

blocks.heading: 四情境走讀
paragraphs: 逐一走讀缺漏、修改、取消與確認匯出。
這裡的四個情境只是一組最小走讀案例，不代表涵蓋所有例外。正式系統仍須依業務風險補充權限不足、資料衝突、外部服務失敗等測試。
如果你的流程遇到某個事件，必須由閱讀者自行發明處理方式，表示需求還沒有定義完整。

sections.heading: 十、總結：這一課真正要帶走的五件事
paragraphs:
1. 先定義同一個任務。 As-Is 與 To-Be 必須具有可比較的角色、起點、終點和範圍。
2. 現況要有證據。 不要把想像中的工作方式直接當成真實 SOP。
3. 改善不等於全面自動化。 需要清楚分配人類與系統的責任。
4. User Flow 不只有成功路徑。 缺漏、修改、取消和失敗後的回復，都要有明確出口。
5. 流程設計是後續軟體開發的依據。 它會影響介面、規格、測試以及系統所需的控制機制。
最後要記住：
好的流程不是框框最少的流程，而是能讓使用者正確完成工作、發生問題時可以回復，而且責任與結果都清楚的流程。

sections.heading: 理解檢核：換一個產業，看你能不能獨立應用
paragraphs: 假設一家公司準備開發 AI 輔助的員工差旅費報銷系統。
目前員工需要手動整理收據、填 Excel，再寄給財務部門。未來希望員工上傳收據後，由 AI 辨識金額與日期，自動整理報銷草稿，再由員工確認並送交財務審核。
請回答以下四題：
參考解析位於文末理解檢核，可自行展開比對；這些問題不代表已提交或通過實務驗收。
能夠獨立回答這四題，尤其能清楚說明「修改後重查」與「失敗後如何回復」，就掌握了 M03-03 最核心的實務能力。

exercise.environment: problem.md、文字編輯器或紙筆，以及四張合成事件卡；不必安裝繪圖軟體。
steps: 為收件任務寫下相同的起點與終點，並標示現況是觀察所得還是待訪談假設。
並排寫 As-Is 與 To-Be，為缺漏、檢查後修改、取消各補回饋與回復點。
請同儕用四張事件卡走讀，記錄一處不明確分支並修改 problem.md；單人自學可自行依卡逐步核對。
exercise.expected: problem.md 具有可比較的兩條流程、主路徑與三個例外分支，以及明確原型邊界。
exercise.check: 能指出缺件如何補回、修改後為何重查，以及哪個終點只代表完整性報告；流程沒有把伺服器當成操作角色。
exercise.cleanup: 保留合成卡與修訂理由；丟棄含真實案件內容的草圖，公開版本只留下合成範例。

openChecks.prompt: Q1｜請定義這個任務的起點、終點，以及哪些業務不在第一版範圍內。
answer: 可將起點定為員工取得待報銷收據，終點為確認後的申請已送交財務並取得可核對紀錄，或取消。第一版可排除財務正式核准、實際撥款與外部會計串接；實際邊界須與利害關係人確認。

openChecks.prompt: Q2｜請各寫出一條 As-Is 和 To-Be 流程，並區分人與 AI 的責任。
answer: As-Is：員工整理收據 → 填 Excel → 寄送財務。To-Be：員工上傳 → AI 辨識並建立草稿 → 員工核對修正 → 系統重查 → 員工確認送交財務。AI 提取資料，員工確認內容，財務保留業務審核責任。

openChecks.prompt: Q3｜假設 AI 讀取收據金額為 1,500 元，員工修改成 15,000 元。原本的檢查結果應該如何處理？為什麼？
answer: 由 1,500 元改成 15,000 元會改變受檢輸入，立即使舊檢查、預覽及通過標記失效，重新檢查後才能送出。輸出須對應目前版本；必要欄位完整仍不能證明金額正確。

openChecks.prompt: Q4｜AI 無法辨識收據、員工取消申請、送出時網路斷線。請分別設計下一步與回復方式。
answer: 無法辨識：標明未辨識欄位並保留上傳與已填資料，允許人工補正後重查。取消：不新增本次申請，草稿保留與否另定。斷線：顯示送出結果未確認，先查申請紀錄／請求識別，再安全重試，避免重複申請。

en.summary: Compare current, intended and exception paths for the same task so recovery, handoff conditions and system boundaries can be discussed step by step.
objectives: Write As-Is and To-Be flows for the same task with roles, a start and an endpoint.
Represent missing input, rechecking after changes and cancellation using a main flow and branch table.
Distinguish user flows, broader journeys and system architecture.

readingGuide.goal: Write As-Is and To-Be flows for the same task with roles, a start and an endpoint.
readingGuide.startingPoint: problem.md, a text editor or paper, and four synthetic event cards; no diagramming software is needed.
readingGuide.route: Read the scenario and principles, compare examples, then expand problem.md and use the checks to review your understanding.
readingGuide.output: Two comparable flows, a main path, three exception branches and an explicit prototype boundary in problem.md.

sections.heading: M03-03 | As-Is, To-Be and User Flow: turning work into useful software
paragraphs: Before developing software, understand how people currently do the work, how they want to do it in future, and what should happen when something goes wrong.
Whether you are developing hospital appointment booking, factory management, an online shop, an internal banking tool or an AI Agent, first understand three concepts:

- As-Is (current workflow): How is this task done now?
- To-Be (target workflow): How should it work better in future?
- User Flow: Which actions, decisions and branches must a user follow in the new system to complete the task?
Their relationship can be expressed in one sentence:
As-Is helps identify problems, To-Be helps design improvements, and User Flow helps check that the proposed approach can actually be followed.
That is why software development cannot begin only with “Should we use React, Python or a particular AI model?” Technology implements the work; first establish what the work requires.

sections.heading: 1. Understand the concepts through everyday work
paragraphs: Suppose you run a restaurant and order ingredients from a supplier every morning.
As-Is: the current way of working
The manager checks the refrigerator, writes missing ingredients on paper and phones the supplier. If nobody answers, the manager must call again later.
Problems: time spent, missed items and incomplete records.
To-Be: the proposed improved way
The manager opens an ordering system showing stock and suggested purchase quantities, confirms the quantities and submits an order. The supplier receives a notification.
Goals: reduce repeated work, lower the chance of missing items and retain records.
User Flow: how will someone actually operate it?
Sign in → check stock → adjust quantities → confirm → submit.
But what if ingredients are unavailable, prices change, the network fails or the manager cancels? Each situation needs an explicit path.

The To-Be above is a design hypothesis, not demonstrated performance improvement. Before launch, check the accuracy of the data, whether the manager will adopt the system and whether the new method adds work.

blocks.caption: Figure 1 · Three views of restaurant ordering
blocks.description: Arrows indicate analysis moving from current work to a target and then explicit operations; improvements remain hypotheses.

items.title: As-Is
items.body: Check the refrigerator → write missing items → phone the supplier; unanswered calls require another attempt. Time, omissions and incomplete records are current concerns.

items.title: To-Be
items.body: Show stock and suggested quantities → manager confirms → submit → notify supplier. Goals are less repeated work, fewer omissions and retained records; notification is not supplier acceptance.

items.title: User Flow
items.body: Sign in → check stock → adjust quantities → confirm → submit. Define branches for unavailable items, changed prices, network failure and cancellation.

paragraphs: This is the purpose of Requirements Engineering: understand whether the system can improve real work, beyond imagining an attractive interface.

sections.heading: 2. Fix the start and endpoint before comparing workflows
paragraphs: Fix the comparison scope before judging whether a workflow improves the task.
Imagine two people comparing travel from Taipei to Kaohsiung.
Person A says, “Driving takes me four hours.”
Person B says, “High-speed rail takes only one and a half hours.”
But A counts the trip from home to the destination, while B counts only time on the train and excludes travel to and from the stations.
These measurements do not support a fair comparison.
The same applies to work processes.
Suppose a hospital wants to improve appointment booking:

blocks.caption: 2. Fix the start and endpoint before comparing workflows | Comparison
rows: Patient decides to book an outpatient appointment
Patient decides to book an outpatient appointment
Phone, ask about times and confirm details
Select specialty and time online, then confirm details
Obtain a valid booking or cancel
Obtain a valid booking or cancel

paragraphs: Both sides must handle the same task before you can reasonably compare time, cost, error rate or completion rate.
If As-Is includes connecting the call, hospital review, check-in and consultation, while To-Be includes only clicking “Book”, the comparison has different boundaries.

blocks.heading: Five elements for defining a task
paragraphs: Task definition = actor + trigger + end state + success condition + scope
For online appointment booking:
Actor: the patient making the appointment.
Trigger: the patient wants to book a particular outpatient visit.
End State: a successful booking with confirmation details, or cancellation.
Success Condition: the system actually creates a valid appointment and the patient can confirm its details.
Scope: booking operations are included; subsequent diagnosis and treatment are excluded.
These five elements form a practical framework, not a mandatory standard.
A “Success” message alone does not establish business success. There must also be corresponding evidence, such as an appointment record actually being created.

sections.heading: 3. As-Is: understand work as it happens
paragraphs: Think of As-Is as a record of work in the field.
Suppose factory equipment faults are handled by maintenance staff:

1. An operator notices abnormal equipment behavior.
2. The operator phones a supervisor.
3. The supervisor contacts maintenance.
4. A maintenance worker assesses the equipment on site.
5. After repair, the worker completes a paper record.
6. The supervisor confirms that the equipment can resume operation.
This is one possible As-Is workflow.
Recording these six steps still leaves important questions unanswered.
What if the supervisor is absent, parts are unavailable or the fault recurs? Who can find the previous record? Could somebody restart the equipment before its safety check is complete?
These apparently small situations often explain why a system is needed.

blocks.heading: How can you establish a credible As-Is?
paragraphs: Build it progressively from three kinds of evidence:

blocks.caption: 3. As-Is: understand work as it happens | Comparison
rows: How work is supposed to happen
How they believe they complete the work
What actually happens and where work gets stuck

paragraphs: Keep observed current practice separate from your assumptions about it.
For example:
“The factory normally requires supervisor approval before requesting maintenance.”
Without interviews, records or a supporting policy, mark this as an assumption to confirm, rather than a verified fact.
This follows GOV.UK's Discovery approach: before committing to construction, understand users' work, existing arrangements, constraints and relationships with other teams.

sections.heading: 4. To-Be: redesign work and allocate responsibility
paragraphs: Suppose the factory maintenance system is about to introduce AI.
An initial suggestion might be:
“Let AI diagnose faults, schedule maintenance and decide when production resumes.”
This assigns responsibilities of very different kinds to AI together.
A more suitable To-Be might be:

blocks.caption: 4. To-Be: redesign work and allocate responsibility | Comparison
rows: AI suggests possible causes and retrieves history

paragraphs: This involves three layers:
First, improve information. Information previously scattered across phone calls, paper and personal memory is presented together.
Second, improve work. The system provides needed information more quickly, reducing repeated manual lookups.
Third, improve decisions. AI can offer suggestions, while authorized people retain responsibility for confirming high-risk decisions.
When designing To-Be, ask:
“Which activities should be removed, simplified, automated or kept with people?”
Also ask whether an existing step is necessary for safety, legal or quality reasons.
Some apparently redundant steps serve necessary purposes. The shortest process is not automatically the right To-Be.

sections.heading: 5. User Flow: make the software operations explicit
paragraphs: The preceding sections describe ways of working.
Now focus on what the user encounters while operating the software.

The lesson uses a field-completeness prototype. The user enters an application number, applicant code and document type. The system checks required fields for omissions and produces a completeness report.
Distinguish these terms:

- Completeness: Are all required fields filled?
- Correctness: Is the entered content correct?
- Authenticity: Is the information genuine and trustworthy?
- Acceptance: Has the business officially accepted the case under its rules?
Checking that all three fields contain values establishes only the specified field-completeness rule. It does not establish correctness or approval.

blocks.heading: Read the workflow diagram
paragraphs: To-Be User Flow: the completeness-checking prototype
The following diagram combines the success path and exception handling.

blocks.caption: Figure 2 · Completeness checking: decisions and recovery
blocks.description: Follow the explicitly named destination at each decision. Return paths retain entered data; editing invalidates the old result. Arrows describe control flow, not elapsed time or business approval.

items.title: Start
items.body: → Enter required fields.

items.title: Enter required fields
items.body: Application number, applicant code and document type → Cancel?

items.title: Cancel?
items.body: Yes → End without a report. No → Check current input.

items.title: Check current input
items.body: → Required fields complete?

items.title: Required fields complete?
items.body: No → Show omissions and retain values. Yes → Preview checked result.

items.title: Show omissions and retain values
items.body: → Enter required fields; correct omissions and check again.

items.title: Preview checked result
items.body: → Edit data?

items.title: Edit data?
items.body: Yes → Invalidate previous result. No → Confirm export?

items.title: Invalidate previous result
items.body: → Enter required fields; a new check is required.

items.title: Confirm export?
items.body: Yes → Export report → Task complete. No/cancel → End without a report.

items.title: Export report → Task complete
items.body: The report corresponds to current checked input; no official acceptance is implied.

items.title: End without a report
items.body: No new report is produced in this task. Draft retention requires a separate decision.

paragraphs: Read the decision conditions and where each outcome leads.

blocks.caption: Common User Flow terminology
rows: Who operates the system or participates in the task
What the user or system does
A condition that determines the next step
How completion works when everything goes as expected
What happens when information is missing or another problem occurs
How to return to a state where work can continue
An explicit outcome such as success, cancellation or failure

paragraphs: The Happy Path describes normal conditions, not all system behavior.
For an online shop:
The normal flow is “choose products → cart → payment → order confirmed”.
Payment failure, insufficient stock, an expired discount code and checkout abandonment must also have defined paths.

sections.heading: 6. Why must editing input invalidate an old result?
paragraphs: This is a central M03-03 design rule and a common source of errors in AI software.
Suppose an insurer has an AI quotation system.
The user first enters:

blocks.caption: Figure 3 · The first quotation input
blocks.description: Synthetic example: these values illustrate which input produced a result; they are not a premium formula.

items.title: Coverage
items.body: TWD 1,000,000 (100 ten-thousand TWD).

items.title: Hypothetical premium
items.body: TWD 12,000 per year.

items.title: Result produced
items.body: Corresponds to the original input. Editing coverage to TWD 3,000,000 invalidates this result.

paragraphs: The user then changes coverage to TWD 3,000,000.
What happens if the screen shows TWD 3,000,000 but the downloaded PDF still contains the old quote for TWD 1,000,000?
The visible input and output document disagree.
This is a Stale Result problem.
Each result must remain tied to the input that produced it; updating the screen alone does not establish that relationship.

blocks.heading: Result invalidation simulation
paragraphs: Edit → invalidate → check again → output.
Express the rule as an implication:
Valid result ⇒ current input matches the validated input.

In practice, a front-end “checked” flag is insufficient. If multiple people or systems can change the data, use backend versions, snapshots or hashes to confirm consistency, and validate again when the operation actually executes.
This principle applies across industries.

blocks.caption: 6. Why must editing input invalidate an old result? | Comparison
rows: A customer changes the loan amount but the report uses old data
Invalidate old calculations and review results
Updated patient data still shows an old risk analysis
Cart edits retain the previous checkout amount
A changed delivery address retains freight based on the old address
Changed task requirements leave the Agent executing an old plan
Recheck the plan and execution authorization

paragraphs: Workflow design therefore connects to software state management, data consistency and safety governance.

sections.heading: 7. User Flow, User Journey and System Architecture
paragraphs: These diagrams answer different questions even though they are often mixed together.
User Flow
Focuses on a specific task: where the user clicks, what they do and how they recover from problems.
Example: how a patient completes one booking on a hospital website.
User Journey / Experience Map
Focuses on a longer experience that can span times, people, places and services.
Example: a patient's experience from feeling unwell and finding a hospital through booking, consultation and follow-up.
System Architecture
Focuses on how technical components collaborate.
Example: how the booking website calls an API, how the database stores appointments, how authentication works and how duplicate bookings are prevented.

blocks.caption: Figure 5 · Different questions, different views
blocks.description: These three views are parallel comparisons, not sequential steps.

items.title: User Flow
items.body: One task: how a patient books once, including clicks, decisions and recovery.

items.title: User Journey / Experience Map
items.body: A longer experience: feeling unwell → finding a hospital → booking → consultation → follow-up, across people, places and services.

items.title: System Architecture
items.body: Technical collaboration: website, API, appointment database, authentication and duplicate-booking controls.

paragraphs: A Swimlane Diagram can additionally separate responsibilities into lanes, such as patient, booking system and hospital reception.
More formal workflows across organizations may use BPMN (Business Process Model and Notation).
You do not need to learn every diagram standard at once.
For this lesson, clearly define what the user needs to accomplish, how they accomplish it and what happens on exceptions.
GOV.UK's Experience Map guide likewise includes users' actions, thoughts and feelings over time and their contact with multiple services, rather than only operations within one system.

sections.heading: 8. Apply the concepts in AI-assisted software engineering
paragraphs: Write the analysis in a requirements document that both people and AI can understand, such as `problem.md`.
This document provides a basis for design, implementation and verification; it is not executable code.
Return to restaurant ordering for a simplified example.

blocks.heading: problem.md
paragraphs: Synthetic example; As-Is awaits interviews and To-Be awaits validation. The shared Chinese problem.md defines the restaurant manager and supplier; starts with an ingredient list and ends with a recorded and sent request or cancellation; excludes supplier acceptance, delivery and payment. Current work is stocktake, handwriting, phoning and recording. The target is selecting ingredients, entering quantities, checking required information, previewing, confirming and recording the submission outcome. Missing input retains values; editing invalidates preview; unconfirmed submission allows safe retry; cancellation sends no new request. Confirm electronic receiving, duplicate-order risk on retry, draft retention after cancellation and how supplier acceptance is established.
blocks.code:
# 任務：建立食材訂貨要求

## 角色
主要使用者：餐廳店長
交接對象：食材供應商

## 任務邊界
起點：店長取得需要訂購的食材清單
終點：訂貨要求已記錄並送出，或取消
不包含：供應商正式接單、送貨與付款

## As-Is（待訪談確認）
1. 店長盤點食材
2. 手寫訂貨清單
3. 打電話提出訂貨要求
4. 記錄已提出的要求

## To-Be（待驗證設計）
1. 選擇食材
2. 輸入訂購數量
3. 系統檢查必填資訊
4. 店長預覽內容
5. 店長確認送出
6. 系統記錄送出結果

## 例外與回復路徑
- 缺漏：提示缺少資訊，保留已填資料
- 修改：使舊預覽失效，重新檢查
- 送出失敗：顯示未確認送出，提供安全重試
- 取消：結束操作，不送出新要求

## 待確認事項
- 供應商能否接收電子訂單？
- 重試是否可能造成重複訂貨？
- 取消後是否保留草稿？
- 供應商接受訂單如何確認？

paragraphs: The document lets you establish the work before choosing a front-end framework, database or AI model.
You can give it to an AI Coding Agent such as OpenCode and ask:

“Use `problem.md` to organize the User Flow, exception scenarios and testable requirements. Do not assume the supplier has accepted the order, and do not expand into official payment functionality before confirming requirements.”
This makes development scope and outcomes easier to control than simply requesting “an intelligent ordering website”.

blocks.heading: From workflow to implementation
paragraphs: Distinguish the shared workflow analysis from the two parallel concerns of interfaces and requirements/tests.

blocks.caption: Figure 6 · From analysis to implementation
blocks.description: As-Is → To-Be → User Flow feeds two parallel design concerns, UI/UX and requirements/tests; both inform implementation, verification and improvement. This is a dependency diagram, not a mandatory waterfall schedule.

items.title: As-Is
items.body: Understand current problems and constraints.

items.title: To-Be
items.body: Design a better way of working.

items.title: User Flow
items.body: Define operations, decisions and exception paths.

items.title: UI / UX
items.body: M04: design usable interfaces.

items.title: Requirements and tests
items.body: M05 / M08: define testable behavior.

items.title: Implementation, verification and improvement
items.body: Architecture, AI Coding, testing and iteration.

paragraphs: Workflow design supplies behavioral requirements that an architecture must satisfy; it does not directly determine the technical architecture.

sections.heading: 9. Check whether you can apply the lesson
paragraphs: A practical acceptance exercise for M03-03 is to walk through several events and check for paths that cannot be followed.

blocks.heading: Four-case walkthrough
paragraphs: Walk through missing input, edits, cancellation and confirmed export.

The four cases are a minimum walkthrough, not every exception. A formal system needs additional tests based on business risk, including insufficient permission, data conflicts and external service failures.
If a reader must invent what should happen after an event, the requirement still needs definition.

sections.heading: 10. Five things to carry into your next design
paragraphs:
1. Define the same task. As-Is and To-Be need comparable actors, starts, endpoints and scope.
2. Establish evidence for current practice. Do not turn an imagined workflow into a factual SOP.
3. Allocate human and system responsibilities clearly; improvement does not require total automation.
4. Define exception exits and recovery for omissions, edits, cancellation and failure, alongside the Happy Path.
5. Use workflows as a basis for interface design, specifications, tests and system controls.
Keep this criterion in mind:
A useful flow lets users complete the work correctly, recover from problems and understand responsibilities and outcomes, rather than simply minimizing the number of boxes.

sections.heading: Understanding check: apply the ideas in another industry
paragraphs: Suppose a company is preparing an AI-assisted employee travel-expense system.

Employees currently organize receipts, fill in Excel and email finance manually. The proposal lets employees upload receipts, has AI recognize amounts and dates and prepare a reimbursement draft, then asks employees to confirm it and submit it to finance for review.
Answer four questions:
Reference explanations can be expanded in the final understanding check. These questions do not establish that a learner has submitted answers or passed practical acceptance.
Answering independently, especially explaining rechecking after an edit and recovery after failure, demonstrates application of the lesson's central concepts.

exercise.environment: problem.md, a text editor or paper, and four synthetic event cards; no diagramming software is needed.
steps: Give the intake task matching start and end conditions, labeling current work as observed or an assumption requiring interviews.
Write As-Is and To-Be side by side. Add feedback and recovery points for missing fields, edits after checking and cancellation.
Ask a peer to walk through the four cards, record one unclear branch and revise problem.md. Independent learners can check each card themselves.
exercise.expected: Two comparable flows, a main path, three exception branches and an explicit prototype boundary in problem.md.
exercise.check: Identify how missing data is corrected, why edits require rechecking and which endpoint means only a completeness report. Do not treat a server as a user role.
exercise.cleanup: Keep synthetic cards and revision reasons. Discard sketches containing actual case data; publish synthetic examples only.

openChecks.prompt: Q1 | Define the start, endpoint and business activities outside the first version's scope.
answer: A possible start is the employee obtaining receipts to claim; the endpoint is a confirmed submission to finance with a verifiable record, or cancellation. The first version may exclude official finance approval, actual payment and external accounting integration. Confirm the real boundaries with stakeholders.

openChecks.prompt: Q2 | Write an As-Is and a To-Be flow, distinguishing human and AI responsibilities.
answer: As-Is: employee organizes receipts → fills Excel → emails finance. To-Be: employee uploads → AI recognizes data and prepares a draft → employee checks and corrects → system rechecks → employee confirms submission to finance. AI extracts data; the employee confirms content; finance retains business-review responsibility.

openChecks.prompt: Q3 | AI reads a receipt as TWD 1,500, and the employee changes it to TWD 15,000. What should happen to the previous check, and why?
answer: Changing TWD 1,500 to TWD 15,000 changes checked input. Immediately invalidate the old check, preview and pass flag; recheck before submission. Output must correspond to the current version. Complete fields still do not establish a correct amount.

openChecks.prompt: Q4 | Define the next step and recovery path for an unreadable receipt, employee cancellation and a network failure during submission.
answer: Unreadable receipt: identify unresolved fields, retain the upload and entered values, allow manual correction and recheck. Cancellation: create no new claim; define draft retention separately. Network failure: show that the submission outcome is unconfirmed, check the claim record/request identity and then retry safely to avoid duplicate claims.
